EUR, converted exactly from EUR millions. OWNERSHIP: Bernard Arnault personally holds 946,055 shares ('in a personal capacity', Board membership as of December 31, 2025); the URD gives no percentage, so pctEconomic is null (for reference only, about 0.19% of the 497,686,940 shares; not disclosed). The relevant holding is the Arnault family group's 49.77% of share capital (65.89% of votes exercisable at Shareholders' Meetings; 65.77% of theoretical votes), recorded in family. That figure includes Christian Dior SE's 42.17%, so Christian Dior SE is not listed separately. Whether Bernard Arnault's personal shares are inside the family-group total is not stated; they are not added. Relation is 'chair' (Chairman and CEO since 1989; reappointed by the Board on April 17, 2025). CDC: the URD gives the CDC Group's 1.24% (and CDC's direct 1%) as of its last threshold crossing on April 16, 2025, not December 31; the group figure is used and the direct 1% is not added to it. Percentages of share capital include the 1,295,928 treasury shares (0.26%) in the denominator. About 900,000 shareholders in total (Euroclear survey, December 2025). BUYBACKS: EUR 1,320.8m paid for 2,550,539 shares bought to be retired (parent-company note 13.1), the same rule as last year: purchases covering bonus share plans (579,981 shares, EUR 320.4m) and the liquidity contract (394,947 shares, round-trip) are not counted as cash returned to shareholders. This ties to §4.1.1 (517,973 shares at an average EUR 585.62 plus 2,032,566 at EUR 500.58, all for 'shares pending retirement'). It includes the EUR 1 billion programme of February–November 2025 (1,899,397 shares; note 16.3) plus 651,142 further shares bought for retirement. For reference: gross purchases of all kinds were 3,525,467 shares, EUR 1,863m (cash impact EUR 1,862m, note 16.3), and the cash-flow statement shows a net 'Acquisition and disposal of LVMH shares' of EUR (1,640)m inside 'Other equity-related transactions'. 2,654,760 shares were retired in 2025. DIVIDENDS: EUR 6,465m paid by LVMH SE; the cash-flow line of EUR (7,123)m also includes EUR 414m paid to minority interests and EUR 244m of tax on intra-group dividends, both excluded. STOCK COMP: Note 17.4 expense of EUR 165m, all bonus share plans (no LVMH Shares expense in 2025). PLAN: the URD describes the 2024 LVMH Shares offer and says employees held the equivalent of less than 1% of the share capital at December 31, 2025, in employee savings plans and as registered bonus shares.

footprint.notes: All figures come from LVMH's 2025 Universal Registration Document (fiscal year ended Dec 31, 2025), filed with the AMF. LVMH reports three single countries (France, United States, Japan), which are in countries, and three remainder regions (Europe excl. France, Asia excl. Japan, Other markets), whose country lists the filing does not define. Each table is its own row, so France, the U.S. and Japan appear three times (stores, employees, operating investments) with different metric keys. The investment table calls the last region 'Other countries', not 'Other markets', and the name is kept as filed. The workforce total (211,552 at Dec 31, 2025, including temporary and non-guaranteed-hours contracts) is a different measure from headcounts reported elsewhere; the URD notes a rationalization of the non-guaranteed-hours workforce in the United States in 2025. Store counts include Sephora (2,242 stores). The URD has no U.S. state breakdown and no taxes-by-country table (a search of the 2025 URD for 'country-by-country', 'tax contribution' and 'taxes paid' found nothing); a separate LVMH tax report was not checked. Vineyard areas are in hectares and appear only in site descriptions. Some site quotes are shortened to text that is contiguous in the PDF's two-column layout.

Shares = 494,606,080 total shares − 743,358,184 gross + 739,382,278 net voting rights (parts signed so they sum to shares) = 494,606,080 − 3,975,906 = 490,630,174 at October 31, 2026. The monthly disclosure states no treasury count. Gross minus net voting rights equals the shares deprived of voting rights, which are the treasury shares: the same identity gives exactly the 1,295,928 treasury shares the 2025 URD reports at December 31, 2025 (744,843,762 theoretical − 743,547,834 exercisable votes). If a stated figure is preferred, the total including treasury shares is 494,606,080 (treasury about 0.8%). Share count fell from 497,686,940 at December 31, 2025 as LVMH retired repurchased shares.
